title: Consolidate missing tracepoints and dashboard heatmap coverage for Console incidents
creator: Priya Iyer
description: Summary: During the capacity/regression incidents on 2026-02-22 and 2026-02-28, the Console team lacked consistent heatmap dashboards and end-to-end tracepoints for request flow across the routing and runtime subsystems. Symptoms included: incomplete spike attribution in dashboards, high request tail latency with no trace linking frontend request IDs to backend kernels, and inability to correlate KV-cache misses with user-facing latency spikes. Objective: instrument missing tracepoints, standardize a dashboard heatmap template, and add alerts to catch coverage regressions before customer impact.
background: Incident references: postmortem-consolidated-2026-02-28 (link: https://confluence.redwood/results/pm-2026-02-28-console-capacity). Observability gaps were identified in the incident review and observed during firefighting: - Missing trace context propagation in the console-to-runtime proxy - Heatmaps were per-server not per-route; aggregations hid hot routes - No dashboard tests or CI gating for coverage; dashboards not instrumented to flag missing metrics
findings: Heatmaps only aggregated by host leading to high variance smoothing
Metrics missing tag 'route' and 'model_variant' causing attribution blindness
No dashboard automated smoke test; missing panels went unnoticed
Alerts only on raw CPU/GPU, not on request-level latency distribution tails
